units: I in cm^-1, q in Å^-1, SLD in 10^-6 Å^-2

A.answer: Spherical block-copolymer micelles: dry PPO core (R ≈ 48 Å, 10 % polydisperse) with a highly hydrated PEO corona (≈ 32 Å, ≈ 89 % D2O, so weak contrast). Concentrated enough for a hard-sphere S(Q) with effective radius ≈ 80 Å (core + corona) and micelle volume fraction ≈ 0.16. Aggregation number ≈ 70 from the core volume. Pitfall: sphere@hardsphere with the core contrast fails (reduced χ² ≈ 50) because one volfraction cannot be both the core and the micelle volume fraction; the corona must be in the model.

B.answer: Rod-like (short wormlike) micelles: cylinder radius ≈ 21 Å, matching the extended C16 chain length (Tanford: 1.5 + 1.265 × 16 ≈ 21.7 Å); length ≈ 800 Å with 30 % polydispersity. Volume fraction of tails ≈ 0.004, matching 15 mM CTAB. Q⁻¹ region between the two Guinier knees.

C.answer: Unilamellar vesicles: core radius ≈ 240 Å (22 % polydisperse), bilayer thickness ≈ 38 Å (typical for DOPC). Q⁻² mid-q region from the thin shell; the bilayer thickness sets the high-q drop. Shell volume fraction ≈ 0.01, matching 10 mg/mL. In the vesicle model, keep scale = 1 and fit volfraction.

D.answer: Dilute polydisperse spheres: R ≈ 110 Å (diameter 22 nm), 12 % Gaussian polydispersity, which smears the minima. Volume fraction ≈ 0.009 (2 wt% / 2.2 g/cm³). High flat background (≈ 0.95 cm⁻¹) from H2O incoherent scattering.

E.answer: Bicontinuous microemulsion (Teubner–Strey): broad peak at Q ≈ 0.022 Å⁻¹, repeat distance d ≈ 260 Å, correlation length ξ ≈ 95 Å (d/ξ ≈ 2.7, a weakly ordered sponge). Q⁻⁴ (Porod) decay from sharp oil–water interfaces. Not a droplet form factor: no Guinier plateau, peak without dilute-particle oscillations. The model depends on volfraction_a only through φ(1 − φ), so 0.45 and 0.55 fit equally well; the card decides which.

F.answer: Polymer coil in good solvent: Rg ≈ 68 Å and power-law exponent ≈ 5/3 (Flory ν = 3/5, swollen coil). I(0) ≈ 0.85 cm⁻¹ is consistent with M ≈ 20 kg/mol via I(0) = φ V Δρ². In polymer_excl_volume, scale is I(0), not a volume fraction.
